source.title: DNNs as Layers of Cooperating Classifiers
source.authors: Marelie Hattingh Davel; Marthinus W. Theunissen; Arnold M. Pretorius; E. Barnard

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no truncation or garbling affects the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test error across network depth and width and relates activation-pattern measurements to generalization, using a different setup from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Those topics appear only in cited work or are not addressed. Figure 2 is the paper's own test-error result; other cited-work statements are not rows.
record.test_reason: The width sweep reports test-error saturation, but does not establish which widths reach zero training error or measure widening beyond that threshold. It therefore cannot test V2's defining condition. Depth scaling and activation-pattern perplexity address different questions, and no other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors demonstrate class-related activation regularities and accurate discrete and continuous node-based classifiers. They suggest that collaboration among these classifiers contributes to generalization, while explicitly acknowledging that they do not directly establish that connection.
record.recipe_differences: Fully connected ReLU MLPs trained with Adam on MNIST and FMNIST; no random-label experiment or interpolation-threshold analysis. The study varies depth and width and measures test error and activation-pattern perplexity.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trends vary with width and depth; the authors say perplexity drops more gradually for FMNIST and more sharply for wider networks. They also report that training choices introducing noise generally increase layer perplexity and reduce hidden-unit saturation, without giving a claim-version test.

fits_no_version.finding: For the tested fully connected MNIST and FMNIST networks, test error initially decreases and then saturates with increasing depth or width. Additional depth does not degrade performance in the reported range.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing fully connected network depth or width can produce a plateau in held-out performance, without establishing behavior beyond the zero-training-error width.

fits_no_version.finding: Sufficiently wide and deep networks have near-maximal within-class activation-pattern perplexity in early layers and near-minimal perplexity in later layers; the transition is sharper for wider networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected image classifiers develop a width-dependent transition from sample-specific to class-specific binary activation patterns across layers.

record.peer_reviewed: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (venue stated in supplied metadata); the supplied paper text labels itself a preprint.
record.problems: The relevant test-error values are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The experiments use only fully connected networks on MNIST and FMNIST, without data augmentation, and do not directly test random-label memorization or the claim's named generalization mechanisms. Three training seeds are stated, but uncertainty estimates are not reported here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were reported. Related work in the Introduction and Section 6 is cited background, not this study's own result.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond the width that achieves zero training error; the defining training-error threshold is not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers, local connectivity, and initialization or learned sparsity effects.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparative ranking against other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted V2 limits_scope verdict is unwarranted: saturation without an established zero-training-error threshold does not qualify the post-threshold claim. The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values, so exact errors and training-error thresholds cannot be recovered.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out accuracy under natural labels.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, and whether test error continues to fall beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance under specified tuning.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: Fully-connected feedforward networks, width 100 nodes per layer
rows.size_stated: 100 nodes per layer; depth varied, results shown up to 10 hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-layer depth and measured test error on MNIST and FMNIST.
rows.note: The text says error initially decreases as depth grows, then performance quickly saturates; increasing depth beyond that does not degrade performance. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Depth scaling does not test V2's width claim. The row's condition lists only MNIST, although its description combines MNIST and FMNIST; separate dataset rows would be needed. Section 3.1 reports saturation without degradation through 20 hidden layers, with results displayed through 10.

rows.subject: Fully-connected feedforward networks, depth 10 hidden layers
rows.size_stated: width varied; 20–200 nodes per layer for FMNIST and 20–120 for MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Varied width and measured test error on MNIST and FMNIST.
rows.locator: Figure 2, right; Section 3.1; Appendix B Figures 9–10
rows.note: The text says increased width leads to a similar saturation in performance. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Neither zero training error nor the interpolation width is established, so test-error saturation cannot be assigned a partial V2 effect. The row combines two datasets while listing only MNIST. Appendix B measures derived subsystem classifiers and does not supply the missing interpolation analysis.

rows.subject: Fully-connected feedforward networks
rows.size_stated: width and depth varied; includes layers as small as 20 nodes
rows.operation_detail: Measured per-layer mean activation-pattern perplexity on test samples while varying network depth and width.
rows.measure: per-layer mean perplexity of binary activation patterns
rows.note: The text reports that perplexity drops across networks, with the drop more gradual for FMNIST and sharper for wider networks; below a width threshold, early-layer perplexity reduces. This is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: Activation-pattern perplexity measures neither magnitude-aware weight sharpness nor any other claim version. Its reported trend is an observed finding, but its state relative to these versions cannot be determined.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MNIST and FMNIST fully connected networks in the tested depth and width sweeps
reader_labels.reason: Test error initially falls and then saturates as depth or width increases, rather than continuing to fall; it does not rise beyond the reported range (R1, R2).
